vsm2.17:96.1:
96. (21) A state that, by means of existingness characterized by presence,
assists a like state by consolidating it, is a presence condition.
vsm2.17:96.2:
A sevenfold summary is laid down for it according to immaterial aggregates, great primaries, mentality-materiality,
consciousness and consciousness-concomitants, great primaries, bases, and physical heart basis,
vsm2.17:96.3:
according as it is said: “The four immaterial aggregates are a condition, as presence condition, for each other.
The four great primaries … are … for each other. At the time of descent into the womb
mentality and materiality are a condition, as presence condition, for each other.
vsm2.17:96.4: States of consciousness and consciousness-concomitants are … for the kinds of materiality originated by consciousness.
vsm2.17:96.5: The four great primaries are … for derived materiality.
vsm2.17:96.6:
The eye base is … for the eye-consciousness element and for the states associated therewith.
The ear base … nose base … tongue base … body base is … for the body-consciousness element … The visible-data base
is … for the eye-consciousness element … The sound base … odour base … flavour base … tangible-data base is a condition,
as presence condition, for the body-consciousness element and for the states associated therewith.
vsm2.17:96.7:
The visible-data base … The sound base … odour base … flavour base … tangible-data base is a condition,
as presence condition, for the mind element and for the states associated therewith.
vsm2.17:96.8:
The materiality with which as their support the mind element and mind-consciousness element occur is a condition, as presence
condition, for the mind element, for the mind-consciousness element, and for the states associated therewith” (Paṭṭh I 6).
vsm2.17:97.1:
97. But in the Question Section, after setting forth conascence, prenascence, postnascence, nutriment, and faculty,
the description is given first under conascence in the way beginning, “One aggregate is a condition,
as presence condition, for three aggregates and for materiality originated thereby” (Paṭṭh I 178).
vsm2.17:97.2: Under prenascence the description is given according to the prenascent eye and so on.
vsm2.17:97.3:
Under postnascence the description is given according to postnascent
consciousness and consciousness-concomitants as conditions for this body.
vsm2.17:97.4:
Under nutriments and faculties respectively the description is given thus:
“Physical nutriment is a condition, as presence condition, for this body,”
vsm2.17:97.5: and “The material life faculty is a condition, as presence condition, for materiality due to kamma performed” (Paṭṭh I 178).
vsm2.17:98.1:
98. (22) Immaterial states that, by their ceasing in contiguity before, assist by giving
opportunity to immaterial states that arise proximately (next) after them are absence conditions,
vsm2.17:98.2:
according as it is said: “States of consciousness and consciousness-concomitants that have ceased in contiguity are a condition,
as absence condition, for present states of consciousness and consciousness-concomitants” (Paṭṭh I 7).
vsm2.17:99.1: 99. (23) Those same states, because they assist by their disappearance, are a disappearance condition,
vsm2.17:99.2:
according as it is said: “States of consciousness and consciousness-concomitants that have disappeared in contiguity
are a condition, as disappearance condition, for present states of consciousness and consciousness-concomitants” (Paṭṭh I 7).
vsm2.17:100.1:
100. (24) The same states that are presence condition, because they assist by their non-disappearance,
should be understood as a non-disappearance condition.
vsm2.17:100.2: Or this dyad is stated as an embellishment of teaching to suit the needs of those who are teachable,
vsm2.17:100.3: just as in the Mātikā of the Dhammasaṅgaṇī the “dissociated-from-cause dyad” is given after the “causeless dyad.”
vsm2.17:101.1: How Ignorance is a Condition for Formations
vsm2.17:101.2:
101. Now, as regards these twenty-four conditions:

“For those of merit ignorance
Is a condition in two ways
And for the next in many ways
But for the last kind only once.”
vsm2.17:102.1:
102. Herein, for those of merit ignorance is a condition in two ways: it is a condition in two ways,
namely, as object condition and as decisive-support condition.
vsm2.17:102.2:
For ignorance is a condition, as object condition, for formations of merit of the sense
sphere at the time of comprehending by means of insight ignorance as liable to destruction and fall;
vsm2.17:102.3:
and it is likewise for those of the fine-material sphere at the time of knowing a confused
mind by means of direct-knowledge consciousness through penetrating others’ minds, and so on.
vsm2.17:102.4:
But it is a condition, as decisive-support condition, in two cases, that is to say, for the sense-sphere formation in one who,
for the purpose of surmounting ignorance, fulfils the various instances of sense-sphere merit-making consisting in giving, etc.,
vsm2.17:102.5: and for the fine-material-sphere formation in one who arouses the fine-material jhānas for the same purpose.
vsm2.17:102.6:
Likewise in one who effects that merit while aspiring to the delight of sense-sphere
becoming and fine-material becoming because he is confused by ignorance.
vsm2.17:103.1: 103. And for the next in many ways: it is a condition for formations of demerit in many ways.
vsm2.17:103.3: As object condition at the time of the arising of greed, etc., contingent upon ignorance;
vsm2.17:103.4: as object-predominance and object-decisive-support respectively at the times of giving importance to ignorance and enjoying it;
vsm2.17:103.5: as decisive-support in one who, being confused by ignorance and unaware of danger, kills living things, etc.;
vsm2.17:103.6:
as proximity, contiguity, proximity-decisive-support, repetition,
absence, and disappearance, for the second impulsion and those that follow;
vsm2.17:103.7:
as root-cause, conascence, mutuality, support, association, presence, and non-disappearance, in one doing
anything unprofitable. It is thus a condition in many ways.
vsm2.17:104.1:
104. But for the last kind only once: it is reckoned as a condition in one way, namely,
as decisive-support condition only, for formations of the imperturbable.
vsm2.17:104.2: But its relation as decisive-support condition should be understood as stated under formations of merit.
vsm2.17:105.1:
No Single Fruit from Single Cause

105. Here it may be asked: But how is this? Is ignorance the only condition for formations, or are there other conditions?
vsm2.17:105.2: What is the position here? For firstly, if it is the only one, there follows the assertion of a single cause;
vsm2.17:105.3:
but then if there are others, the description of it as a single cause, namely, “With ignorance
as condition there are formations,” is incorrect—It is not incorrect.
vsm2.17:105.6:
“Nor from a single cause arise
One fruit or many, nor one fruit from many;
’Tis helpful, though, to utilize
One cause and fruit as representative.”
vsm2.17:106.1: 106. Here there is no single or multiple fruit of any kind from a single cause, nor a single fruit from multiple causes,
vsm2.17:106.2: but only multiple fruit from multiple causes.
vsm2.17:106.3:
So from multiple causes, in other words, from temperature, earth, seed, and moisture, is seen to arise
a multiple fruit, in other words, the shoot, which has visible form, odour, taste, and so on.
vsm2.17:106.4:
But one representative cause and fruit given in this way, “With ignorance as condition there
are formations; with formations as condition, consciousness,” have a meaning and a use.
vsm2.17:107.1:
107. For the Blessed One employs one representative cause and fruit when it is suitable for the sake
of elegance in instruction and to suit the idiosyncrasies of those susceptible of being taught.
vsm2.17:107.2:
And he does so in some instances because it is a basic factor, and in some instances because it
is the most obvious, and in some instances because it is not common to all.
vsm2.17:107.3: In the passage “With contact as condition, feeling” (M I 261) he mentions a single cause and fruit because they are basic factors.
vsm2.17:107.4:
For contact is the basic cause of feeling since the kinds of feeling are defined
according to the kinds of contact as “eye-contact-born feeling” and so on,
vsm2.17:107.5: and feeling is contact’s basic fruit since contact is defined according to the kinds of feeling that it produces.
vsm2.17:107.6: He mentions a single cause in the passage “Disease due to phlegm” (A V 110) because that is the most obvious.
vsm2.17:107.7: For here what is obvious is the phlegm, not the kamma, etc., mentioned later in the same sutta.
vsm2.17:107.8:
He mentions a single cause in the passage “Bhikkhus, any states whatever that are unprofitable
are all rooted in unwise attention” (cf. S V 91) because it is not common to all.
vsm2.17:107.9:
For unwise attention to unprofitable things is not common to all states in the way
that, say, physical basis and object are common to all.
vsm2.17:108.1: Consequently, although other causes of formations such as physical basis and object, conascent states, etc., are actually existent,
vsm2.17:108.3: and again because it is the most obvious, “Not knowing, bhikkhus, in ignorance, he forms the formation of merit” (cf. S II 82);
vsm2.17:108.4: and lastly because it is not common to all.
vsm2.17:108.5: So the use of one representative cause and fruit should in each instance be understood according to this explanation of it.
vsm2.17:109.1:
109. Here it may be said: “We admit that. But ignorance is reprehensible and has entirely undesirable fruit.
How then can it rightly be a condition for formations of merit and of the imperturbable?
vsm2.17:109.2: Sugarcane does not grow from bitter nimba seeds.”
vsm2.17:109.3: Why should it not be right?
vsm2.17:109.4: For in the world that is, even among thinkers outside the Dispensation it is recognized that
vsm2.17:109.5:
“Both as opposed and unopposed
A state’s conditions may be found,
And both as like and unlike too:
That does not make it their result.”
vsm2.17:110.1:
110. It is established in the world that when states have a condition, it may
be opposed or unopposed to them as to presence, individual essence, function, and so on.
vsm2.17:110.2: For a preceding consciousness is a condition, opposed as to presence, for the succeeding consciousness;
vsm2.17:110.3: and the preceding training is a condition likewise for the plying of crafts, etc., which take place subsequently.
vsm2.17:110.4: Kamma is a condition, opposed as to individual essence, for materiality; and so are milk, etc., for curds, and so on.
vsm2.17:110.5: Light is a condition, opposed as to function, for eye-consciousness; and so are molasses, etc., for intoxicants, and so on.
vsm2.17:110.6: But eye-cum-visible-data, etc., are respectively a condition, unopposed as to presence, for eye-consciousness, and so on.
vsm2.17:110.7:
And the first impulsion, and those that follow, are a condition, unopposed as to individual
essence and function, for the impulsions that follow them.
vsm2.17:110.8: And just as conditions operate as opposed and unopposed, so also they operate as like and unlike.
vsm2.17:110.9:
Materiality—for example, temperature and nutriment—is a condition for materiality:
the like for the like. And so are paddy seeds, etc., for paddy crops, and so on.
vsm2.17:110.10: The material is a condition for the immaterial, and so is the immaterial for the material: the unlike for the like.
vsm2.17:110.11:
And so are ox hair and ram’s hair, horns, curd, and sesame flour, etc.,
respectively for dabba grass, reeds, bhūtanaka grass, and so on.
vsm2.17:110.12:
And those states for which these are the opposed and unopposed, like and unlike,
conditions are not the results of these states as well.
vsm2.17:111.1: 111. So although this ignorance has entirely undesirable fruit for its result and is reprehensible in its individual essence,
vsm2.17:111.2:
yet it should be understood as a condition, opposed or unopposed and like or unlike as the case may
be, as to presence, function, and individual essence, for all these formations of merit, etc.
vsm2.17:111.3: And its state as a condition has already been given in the way beginning,
vsm2.17:111.4:
“For when unknowing—in other words, ignorance—of suffering, etc., is unabandoned in a man, owing firstly to his unknowing
about suffering and about the past, etc., then be believes the suffering of the round of rebirths to be pleasant
vsm2.17:111.5: and he embarks upon the three kinds of formations, which are the cause of that very suffering” (§62).
vsm2.17:112.1: 112. Moreover, there is this way of explanation as well:
vsm2.17:112.2:
“Now, when a man is ignorant
Of death and rebirth and the round,
The characteristics of the formed,
Dependently-arisen states,
vsm2.17:112.3:
And in his ignorance he forms
Formations of this triple kind,
Then ignorance itself will be
Condition for each of the three.”
vsm2.17:113.1: 113. But how does a man who is confused about these things perform these three kinds of formations?
vsm2.17:113.2: Firstly, when he is confused about death, instead of taking death thus, “Death in every case is break-up of aggregates,”
vsm2.17:113.3: he figures that it is a lasting being that dies, that it is a lasting being’s transmigration to another incarnation, and so on.
vsm2.17:114.1: 114. When he is confused about reappearance, instead of taking rebirth thus, “Birth in every case is manifestation of aggregates,”
vsm2.17:114.2: he figures that it is a lasting being’s manifestation in a new body.
vsm2.17:115.1: 115. When he is confused about the round of rebirths, instead of taking the round of rebirths as pictured thus:
vsm2.17:115.2:
“The endless chain of aggregates,
Of elements, of bases too,
That carries on unbrokenly
Is what is called ‘the round of births,’”
vsm2.17:115.3: he figures that it is a lasting being that goes from this world to another world, that comes from another world to this world.
vsm2.17:116.1:
116. When he is confused about the characteristics of formations, instead of apprehending
their specific and general characteristics,
vsm2.17:116.2: he figures that formations are self, belong to a self, are lasting, pleasant, beautiful.
vsm2.17:117.1:
117. When he is confused about dependently-arisen states, instead of taking
the occurrence of formations to be due to ignorance, etc.,
vsm2.17:117.2:
he figures that it is a self that knows or does not know, that acts and causes action, that appears in rebirth-linking, and he
figures that atoms, an Overlord, etc., shape its body in the various states of the embryo and endow it with faculties,
vsm2.17:117.3:
and that when it has been endowed with faculties it touches, feels, craves,
clings, and endeavours, and that it becomes anew in the next becoming;
vsm2.17:117.4: or he figures thus, “All beings … are moulded by fate, coincidence and nature” (D I 53).
vsm2.17:118.1:
118. Thus he figures, blinded by ignorance. He is like a blind man who wanders about the earth, encountering
now right and now wrong paths, now heights and now hollows, now even and now uneven ground,
vsm2.17:118.2: and so he forms formations now of merit, now of demerit, now imperturbable.
vsm2.17:119.2:
“As one born blind, who gropes along
Without assistance from a guide,
Chooses a road that may be right
At one time, at another wrong,
vsm2.17:119.3:
So while the foolish man pursues
The round of births without a guide,
Now to do merit he may choose
And now demerit in such plight.
vsm2.17:119.4:
But when the Dhamma he comes to know
And penetrates the truths besides,
Then ignorance is put to flight
At last, and he in peace may go.”
